Getting a Root Canal

A 1-minute patient guide with narration. Press space to pause.

Patient guide

Getting a root canal.

Here is what to expect, start to finish.

Inside your tooth.

Under the enamel is soft tissue called the pulp. It runs down through narrow canals inside each root.

Why a root canal?

When deep decay or a crack lets bacteria reach the pulp, it can become infected and painful.

You'll be comfortable.

We numb the area first. You will feel pressure, but you should not feel pain.

Cleaning it out.

Through a small opening, we remove the infected pulp, then clean and shape each canal.

Filled and sealed.

The canals are filled with a rubber-like material called gutta-percha, and the opening is sealed.

Protected with a crown.

Most back teeth get a crown afterward to keep the treated tooth strong.

Easy to care for.

Your tooth may feel tender for a few days. Avoid chewing hard foods on it until it is fully restored.

Brush twice a dayFloss dailyKeep your follow-up visit

Questions? Just ask.

Your dental team is happy to walk you through every step before, during, and after your visit.
